Knowing Learners & Building Classroom Co.lead: School records tell only part of the story, so effective teachers pair them with informal ways of knowing students.

beats: The teacher is the one analyzed.

Knowing Learners & Building Classroom Co.lead: Rigorous instruction works best when it affirms students' cultural identities instead of treating them as deficits.
beats: The room and curriculum reflect students.
Community wealth is a teaching asset.

Knowing Learners & Building Classroom Co.lead: Students take academic risks only when the classroom's relationships make it possible to do so.

Knowing Learners & Building Classroom Co.lead: A student's struggle may reflect language or instruction rather than disability, and gifted students can be overlooked too.
beats: RtI supports first, never delays evaluation.

Knowing Learners & Building Classroom Co.lead: A warm classroom with lowered expectations fails New York's framework, which pairs affirmation with rigor.
beats: Every identity belongs in the room.

Inclusive, Evidence-Based Instruction &.lead: UDL builds flexibility into the lesson from the start instead of retrofitting accommodations afterward.

Inclusive, Evidence-Based Instruction &.lead: In New York, state law protects students of all genders and orientations, and daily classroom habits carry it out.

Language Acquisition Foundations.lead: Silence from a new English learner is a normal stage, not a problem to penalize.

beats: Language difference is not a disability.

Literacy & Language Development for ELLs.lead: Scaffolds give ELLs access to grade-level work now and are withdrawn as competence grows.

New sounds and scripts take learning.
Home-language literacy is a head start.

ELL Assessment, Program Models & Collabo.lead: Working with ENL colleagues is a regulatory expectation, and it cannot override the state exit criteria.

ELL Assessment, Program Models & Collabo.lead: An ELL with a disability keeps language services and gains special education, with neither replacing the other.

Disability Characteristics & Individuali.lead: A disability category suggests typical supports, but the IEP, not the label, drives daily instruction.

Disability Characteristics & Individuali.lead: An IEP only works when its goals and services show up in everyday classroom instruction.

Disability Characteristics & Individuali.lead: Accommodations change how a student learns, while modifications change what the student is expected to learn.
beats: A 504 plan does not reduce mastery.

Disability Characteristics & Individuali.lead: Assistive technology belongs in the daily classroom routine, not only in the therapy room.

AT runs from low to high tech.
The district provides, the teacher embeds.
Adaptive equipment belongs in general education.
Trial data informs the CSE review.

Disability Characteristics & Individuali.lead: RtI is a prevention framework, not a reason to make a student wait for an evaluation.
beats: RtI is required for early reading.
Lack of instruction is not a disability.

Disability Characteristics & Individuali.lead: Students with disabilities learn alongside nondisabled peers unless the IEP justifies a removal.

Disability Characteristics & Individuali.lead: Each classification has predictable needs, yet the IEP, not the label, decides the supports a student gets.

Speak to the student, not the interpreter.
Brain injury plans change with recovery.
Give wait time, not finished sentences.
Gifted students can also have disabilities.

Disability Characteristics & Individuali.lead: Testing accommodations change how a student is tested, never what the test measures.
beats: Accommodations leave the measured skill intact.
Alternate assessment is for severe disabilities.

Disability Law, RtI/PBIS & the CSE Proce.lead: IDEA eligibility takes more than a classification: the disability must also create a need for special education.

Evaluations must be fair and recurring.

beats: A 504 Plan lists accommodations, not goals.
General education teachers must deliver it.

Disability Law, RtI/PBIS & the CSE Proce.lead: Sharing a student's disability information with a colleague who does not serve the student violates FERPA.

Parents are told when records can go.
DASA does not loosen disclosure limits.

Disability Law, RtI/PBIS & the CSE Proce.lead: Tiered supports address academics and behavior, but they may never delay a special education evaluation.
beats: RtI data can replace the discrepancy model.

Disability Law, RtI/PBIS & the CSE Proce.lead: The CSE process runs on written referrals, parental consent, and firm timelines.
beats: The CSE is a multidisciplinary team.
Everything starts with a written referral.

Disability Law, RtI/PBIS & the CSE Proce.lead: General education teachers carry responsibilities at every stage, from Tier 1 instruction to IEP implementation.
beats: Teachers supply data for the evaluation.
Share only with a legitimate interest.
A parent's request is always honored.

Disability Law, RtI/PBIS & the CSE Proce.lead: Removing a student with a disability for more than ten school days triggers special protections.
beats: Short removals follow the usual rules.

Manifestation brings an FBA, with exceptions.
The FBA finds function, the BIP plans.
New York tightly limits restraint and timeout.
Teachers collect data and implement the plan.

Collaboration, Assistive Technology & Se.lead: In consultation, the special educator advises the classroom teacher rather than teaching the students directly.
beats: Collaboration is wide, sharing is limited.

Collaboration, Assistive Technology & Se.lead: New York's continuum runs from least to most restrictive, and placement moves only as needs require.

ICT pairs two teachers in one class.
Special class ratios match student need.
Placement follows the individual student's needs.

Collaboration, Assistive Technology & Se.lead: Assistive technology can be as simple as a pencil grip, and the IEP team must consider it.

The general educator embeds the device.
Universal design does not replace devices.

Collaboration, Assistive Technology & Se.lead: In an ICT class the special educator is a co-instructor with teaching responsibilities, never an aide.

Collaboration, Assistive Technology & Se.lead: Relying too heavily on a 1:1 aide can reduce peer interaction and foster prompt dependence.
beats: Too much aide support can backfire.

Collaboration, Assistive Technology & Se.lead: Teachers must implement the IEP as written, because a material failure to implement can deny FAPE.
beats: The general educator sits on the CSE.

beats: IDEA guarantees FAPE and prior notice.

Teacher Responsibilities: Legal & Ethica.lead: A noncustodial parent keeps FERPA rights unless a court order specifically revokes them.

Teacher Responsibilities: Legal & Ethica.lead: Resolving bullying informally does not replace the oral and written reports DASA requires of teachers.

Teacher Responsibilities: Legal & Ethica.lead: Telling the principal does not satisfy a teacher's personal duty to report suspected abuse.

Telling the principal is not enough.
Report in good faith, never investigate.
School employee allegations follow another law.

Teacher Responsibilities: Legal & Ethica.lead: Appropriate advocacy uses documentation and the chain of command, not unilateral defiance or public disclosure.

Advocacy uses accurate reports and proper channels.
Student welfare is the primary obligation.

Teacher Responsibilities: Legal & Ethica.lead: Parents hold consent, notice, and records rights, and teachers must communicate in a language they understand.
beats: Parents must be able to understand.
Document contacts and reach out early.

Teacher Responsibilities: Legal & Ethica.lead: Teachers follow the code of conduct and route serious discipline to administrators, never imposing unofficial penalties.

Physical restraint is for emergencies only.

Teacher Responsibilities: Legal & Ethica.lead: The Code of Ethics guides professional judgment, while discipline of educators proceeds through separate processes.

The best response puts students first.
Complaints and concerns use proper channels.

Teacher Responsibilities: Legal & Ethica.lead: Chronic absenteeism counts excused absences too, and the teacher's first move is early, nonpunitive outreach.

School-Home Relationships & Family Engag.lead: Families disengage when the only contact from school is reactive or punitive.

School-Home Relationships & Family Engag.lead: A parent's deference or absence from the building may reflect cultural norms, not disengagement.

School-Home Relationships & Family Engag.lead: A conference should never be the first time a family hears about a serious concern.

School-Home Relationships & Family Engag.lead: A parent who chats comfortably in English may still not fully understand a progress report or IEP.

School-Home Relationships & Family Engag.lead: Family engagement means real input into decisions, not just receiving information from the school.

School-Home Relationships & Family Engag.lead: Families need specific strategies they can use at home, not generic advice like read more.

School-Home Relationships & Family Engag.lead: If the same few parents fill every seat, the school is not reaching all families.
